conceptual assets.information: The authentication-valid state determines whether debug accesses and hart-control outputs are enabled. It is produced by the optional authenticator rather than carried as a data value directly from a unit input.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The authenticator produces auth.valid at line 745, or ties it active when authentication is disabled at line 754, and the state controls authenticated access and hart-control behavior at lines 212-213, 500 and 505, so corruption can compromise authorization integrity.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could influence the authentication exchange or validity path to make an unauthenticated requester appear valid or to hold the module permanently invalid, respectively granting unauthorized debug control or denying authorized operation.

conceptual assets.information: The selected-hart setting identifies which hart receives debug control requests and whose status is reported. Debug operation depends on applying commands and status accesses to the intended hart.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: A DMI write stores the hart-selection value at line 429, and the resulting selection drives hart targeting through lines 487 and 500, so unauthorized modification can redirect debug control to another hart.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write a different hart selection so halt, resume, reset-status, or debug operations affect the wrong hart and fail to control the intended one.

conceptual assets.information: The data-register contents are words exchanged with a hart during abstract debug accesses. Abstract reads and writes depend on retaining this data between DMI or bus accesses and the hart-side debug transfer.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The data register can be overwritten from DMI or bus input data at lines 666 and 668, allowing unauthorized modification of a hart debug transfer.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could read the data register through a DMI or bus response or overwrite it before a hart transfer, exposing or corrupting debugged data.

conceptual assets.information: The halt request is the command asserted to stop the selected hart. Debug control depends on preserving and delivering this request to the hart-control boundary.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: DMI data writes the halt command state at line 426 and the selected, authenticated command drives halt_req_o at line 500, so unauthorized modification can assert or suppress hart halting.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the debug control value or its gating conditions to halt an unintended hart or prevent the intended hart from being halted.

conceptual assets.information: The busy state indicates that the debug command controller is executing an abstract command. It gates acceptance of new command, program-buffer, data, and auto-execution accesses and is reported through debug status.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The controller remains busy until the selected hart acknowledges completion at lines 305-306, so withholding or corrupting the completion path can block subsequent debug operations.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force the controller to appear idle during an active command or keep it busy by preventing completion, causing unsafe overlap or denial of later debug accesses.

considered, not kept.reason: The debug-module rule bars authentication exchange words that only hold or decide what the debug ports deliver, so this is not a separate conceptual asset here.
The command register is a debug-module command word used to sequence and report debug operations, and the debug-module rule bars it from being a piece of its own.
The program-buffer words and their generated instruction copy only determine what the debug ports deliver to the hart, so the debug-module rule bars a separate concept for them.
The auto-execution, active, and related debug-control register fields only gate or sequence debug-port operations and are barred by the debug-module rule.

considered, not kept.concept: Hart halt, resume, reset, and status bookkeeping
considered, not kept.reason: The internal hart status, resume, reset, and acknowledgment fields only hold or report debug operations through the debug port and are not spared by the debug-module rule.

considered, not kept.concept: Command sequencing state and error status
considered, not kept.reason: The state machine, illegal-command flags, and command-error status are sequencing or debug status information barred by the debug-module rule; the separately spared busy state is kept as C5.
The ndmreset setting and ndmrstn_o only combine and pass a reset request, which the clocks-and-resets rule excludes from conceptual assets.

Although a busy flag is spared for usual judgement, auth.busy is only reported at line 550 and does not gate, block, or alter a protected operation in this RTL, so no objective and violation mechanism support keeping it.
The access command fields and response handshakes only carry or qualify register and data accesses, so the access-command and transfer rules provide no independent conceptual asset.
The instruction contents are a build-time constant at lines 149-182 that no runtime element can modify or withhold as a protected asset.
clk_i and rstn_i only time or reset the unit and its authenticator, and the clocks-and-resets rule excludes them.
